payload.root_cause: `tag_orders` in pyshop/reports.py uses a mutable default argument, `existing: list = []` (line 23). Python creates this default list once at function-definition time, and it is shared across all calls that omit the argument. Because the function aliases it (`result = existing`, line 25) and appends to it in place (`result.append(order['id'])`, line 28) instead of building a fresh list, every call without an explicit `existing` accumulates ids into the same persistent list. The first call `tag_orders(ORDERS, 'gift')` mutates the shared default to ['o1','o3']; the subsequent call `tag_orders(ORDERS, 'rush')` appends 'o3' to that same list, returning ['o1','o3','o3'] instead of ['o3']. This also violates the docstring, which promises a new list when `existing` is not given, and as a side effect it mutates any caller-supplied list in place.

payload.rationale: The root cause is the mutable default argument `existing: list = []`, which is created once at function-definition time and shared across all calls that omit it. Because `result = existing` aliases that shared list and `result.append(...)` mutates it in place, the first call (`tag_orders(ORDERS, 'gift')` -> ['o1','o3']) poisons the default, so the second call (`tag_orders(ORDERS, 'rush')`) returns ['o1','o3','o3']. The fix replaces the mutable default with `None` and creates a fresh list via `result = existing if existing is not None else []` when no list is supplied. This satisfies the docstring ('a new list otherwise') and the test `test_tag_orders_fresh_list_each_call`, while preserving the documented appending behavior when `existing` IS supplied (test_tag_orders_appends_to_existing expects ['o0','o3']).
